answer: A task-bounty ledger pays 1 credit per completed job: locating the zenith in a sky image, transcribing a sonnet, or identifying a raven call. Each commissioned input has one public task ID and a fixed validation test; only the first valid result can redeem its bounty. The ledger marks that ID spent atomically, regardless of submitter key. Reposting the same result through 100 aliases earns no extra credits; more pay requires solving different tasks. This limits reward duplication, but cannot prevent stolen answers winning the race.
